item_prompt: For this scenario, state (1) the strongest evidence-based conclusion and (2) one concrete reason or missing/present evidence that makes it justified. Answer each part in one sentence.

scoring.facet_conclusion: one point if conclusion is materially consistent with reference; reject contrary categorical claims
scoring.facet_evidence: one point if a specific reason or verification boundary is correctly explained; do not award for repeating the conclusion
scoring.missing: missing/not_scored, never imputed as zero without prespecified rule
scoring.double_rating: For any later consented study, two independent, condition-blinded human raters on a locked rubric; report agreement and adjudicate discrepancies; rubric has not been calibrated.
scoring.key_visibility: PUBLIC development examples, no blinded validity

constraints: No actual participants, iPhone collection, contact, browser tracking, researcher auto-grading, delayed retest or data storage.

items.scenario: A public monitoring site displays a receipt confirming that a backup request for laptop L17 entered its queue. No laptop scheduler entry or local execution result is available.
items.reference_conclusion: The remote queue acknowledgement is supported, but unattended execution on laptop L17 is not verified.
items.reference_reason: A machine-specific scheduler record and its execution result would be needed, correlated to the receipt.
facet_evidence_accept: Machine-specific scheduler or execution evidence missing
Match that evidence to the receipt
common_invalid_claims: Claiming the laptop definitely completed the backup

items.scenario: A nonprofit first receives donor pledges. Later, its bank statement shows a settled deposit from the payment processor for those pledges.
items.reference_conclusion: A confirmed deposit supports that the nonprofit received funds; the earlier pledges alone did not.
items.reference_reason: The settlement/bank credit is stronger payment evidence than donor promises or authorizations.
facet_conclusion_accept: Received funds supported by posted deposit
Pledge is not the settled payment
facet_evidence_accept: Bank settlement or confirmed credit is present
common_invalid_claims: Only the pledge proves the cash arrived

items.scenario: A developer claims that a function outputs an even number for every permitted integer. The function outputs 7 on one permitted input.
items.reference_conclusion: The universal even-output claim is false.
items.reference_reason: One valid permitted input with an odd output is a counterexample to an all-input claim.
facet_evidence_accept: Odd output on permitted input is a valid counterexample
common_invalid_claims: Thousands of earlier passes preserve the universal claim

items.scenario: A software team keeps a crash report for version A, a change log for its fix in version B, and a passing rerun result for version B.
items.reference_conclusion: The team has preserved a reconstructable failure-to-repair trail.
items.reference_reason: The original failure, version-specific correction and rerun remain linked rather than overwritten.
facet_conclusion_accept: Traceable history or audit trail preserved
facet_evidence_accept: Original failure and linked source revisions/retest retained
common_invalid_claims: The original failure is unnecessary once the fix passes

items.scenario: A freelance client has signed a contract, approved an invoice, and initiated a card charge. The payment processor still labels the transfer pending.
items.reference_conclusion: The records support an agreement and pending payment, not verified cash received.
items.reference_reason: Settlement or a confirmed bank credit is not present, despite contract and authorization evidence.

items.scenario: A workstation has a timestamped scheduled task record identifying that host. Its wrapper reports a run outcome tied to the same request ID as a server receipt.
items.reference_conclusion: The combined records support stronger attribution to a specific scheduled workstation run than the receipt alone.
items.reference_reason: The host-local scheduled record, wrapper result and remote receipt can be correlated; their authenticity and limits still matter.
facet_evidence_accept: Correlated scheduler, wrapper and remote receipt
No unconditional claim of perfect proof
common_invalid_claims: A public receipt alone would offer equal attribution

items.scenario: A game patch fails a test. The team archives that failure, commits the repair with a new revision ID, and links a successful rerun.
items.reference_conclusion: The failure and repair sequence is recoverable and auditable.
items.reference_reason: The archived failing result, changed revision and successful retest form an evidence chain.
facet_evidence_accept: Preserved failed result plus revision identity and rerun
common_invalid_claims: A later pass replaces the historical failure

items.scenario: A forecasting script passes 80,000 finite input tests. Its author now claims the script is correct for every possible allowed input.
items.reference_conclusion: The finite tests support only the checked cases, not the unrestricted universal claim.
items.reference_reason: Finite successes alone do not establish all possible inputs; a general proof or valid refuting example is a different form of evidence.
facet_conclusion_accept: Universal assertion not established by sample
facet_evidence_accept: Finite testing does not cover all allowed cases
common_invalid_claims: 80,000 passing tests logically prove all cases

items.scenario: A building simulation predicts that every permitted loading pattern is safe. A later test with a genuinely permitted pattern shows a structural failure.
items.reference_conclusion: The universal safety prediction has been refuted.
items.reference_reason: The valid failing load is a counterexample even if many other tested patterns passed.
facet_evidence_accept: One genuine allowed failure is sufficient as counterexample
common_invalid_claims: More previous passes erase the failing case

items.scenario: Two cloud agents independently display 'completed' with the same ticket ID for a job intended for a named Windows computer. No on-device scheduler or run evidence is presented.
items.reference_conclusion: The cloud reports may show status agreement but do not prove execution on that Windows computer.
items.reference_reason: Host-specific execution records are absent; copied or agreed messages cannot authenticate local unattended work.
facet_evidence_accept: Need local scheduler or run record linked to ticket
common_invalid_claims: Same ticket shown twice proves computer execution

items.scenario: An engineer publishes a repaired version of a script, but deletes the original failing log and removes the identifier for the source version that failed.
items.reference_conclusion: The historical trail is incomplete despite the repaired script.
items.reference_reason: The original failed observation and its source identity can no longer be reconstructed from the remaining record.
facet_evidence_accept: Missing original failure and version linkage
common_invalid_claims: Working new version restores the deleted old evidence

items.scenario: A small retailer's payout statement lists a transfer as scheduled for tomorrow. The business bank account has not yet credited the deposit.
items.reference_conclusion: A payout is scheduled but receipt in the bank is not yet confirmed.
items.reference_reason: A scheduled transfer is a promise/process state; confirming a posted bank credit is stronger evidence of receipt.
common_invalid_claims: A scheduled payout is already settled cash
